title: WPMS/300/2003 of SAMAY SINGH andV ORS. Vs DHEER SINGH and ORS.

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.300 of 2003 (M/S)
Samay Singh and Ors.
Ö Petitioner
Vs.
Dheer Singh & Ors.
ÖRespondents
Mr. Sharad Sharma, Sr. Advocate assisted by Mrs. Indu Sharma, Advocate for
the petitioner
Mr. A.K. Sharma, Advocate for private respondent
Honíble B.S.Verma, J. (Oral)
By means of this writ petition, the petitioner has
prayed to set aside the order dated 17.4.2003 passed by
Deputy Director of Consolidation, District Haridwar,
whereby learned D.D.C. has amended Chak road and
proceeded to allocate chak road from west to east side.
Brief facts of the case are that respondent no.1
Dheer Singh filed objections u/s 21(1) of the
Consolidation of Holdings Act, 1953 before the
Consolidation Officer to amend chak road from western
side to eastern side. Learned Consolidation Officer
rejected the objections of respondent no.1. Being
aggrieved, respondent no.1 preferred an appeal which was
also dismissed vide order dated 27.12.2002 passed by
Settlement Officer Consolidation. Further aggrieved, the
petitioner filed a revision u/s 48 of the Act. After hearing
the parties, learned Deputy Director of Consolidation
allowed the revision vide impugned order dated 17.4.2003
and observed that by amending chak road from western
side to eastern side no prejudice is going to be caused to
any other tenure holder. The respondent of chak no.278
is having chak road and Nali towards the west side of

2
their chak and other tenure holders are also having chak
road on their chaks. If chak mark is amended, no tenure
holder would be affected and villagers will also get its
benefit. Feeling aggrieved by the judgment and order of
learned Deputy Director of Consolidation, the petitioner
has filed the present writ petition.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
In my opinion, the petitioner is not going to be
affected by amendment of chak road. Impugned judgment
and order does not suffer from any manifest error of law
and therefore no interference is required.
The writ petition lacks merit and is dismissed
accordingly.
 (B.S.Verma,J.)
 24.10.2013
Rajni
